title: Adapter request definitions
description: The values the adapter's requests and their answers share, by name under $defs: adapter.schema.json, source-collections.schema.json, source-items.schema.json, source-item-comments.schema.json, sources-disconnect.schema.json, connections-disconnect.schema.json, changes.schema.json, changes-failed.schema.json, changes-submitted.schema.json, connect-pass.schema.json, connect-return.schema.json, setup-pass.schema.json, adapter-secrets.schema.json, adapter-secrets-answer.schema.json, adapter-secrets-plaintext.schema.json, grant.schema.json, grant-end.schema.json, grants.schema.json, run-credential.schema.json, resolve.schema.json, resolve-answer.schema.json, read.schema.json and read-answer.schema.json refer to them. description.schema.json refers to secret_name, for its source role. description.schema.json refers to endpoint_url, model_id and effort_value, for its model_provider role, and to change_kind, for its source role. An adapter is the program that reads a source of work, such as a tracker, and reports what is in that source to the control plane. Every POST body is application/json; a GET has no body. An integer is written without a fraction or an exponent, and no object repeats a member, at any depth; the control plane refuses either, 400 invalid_request. The numbers inside the description member of POST /v1/adapter follow description.schema.json instead, and may have a fraction or an exponent; no object inside it repeats a member either. The numbers inside the data member of a change_request entry and of a changes-submitted reply follow the schema of the change's kind instead, and may have a fraction or an exponent; no object inside them repeats a member either. Every request is signed with the adapter's access key as github.com/qoryai/forager/accesskey signs a request (Request.Message, Key.SignRequest): the headers X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Contract-Version and X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519, the signature over qory-request-ed25519-v1, the access key id, the instance id, the method, the target and, for a GET, X-Qory-Timestamp, which it also sends, or, for a POST, the raw body, whose time is checked for freshness. X-Qory-Contract-Version is the revision of this contract the adapter implements, a decimal integer; the control plane refuses one that is missing, sent twice, not a decimal integer, or a revision it does not serve, 400 unsupported_contract_version. The control plane's answer contains only the members that the named revision defines. The change feed contains only the entry kinds that the named revision defines. An entry of a kind that a higher revision defines is skipped for that adapter and not sent. The feed's cursor still moves past it, so a replay from the start stays in step. The header alone does not select what an adapter accepts. Every answer whose content the revision bounds contains that revision in its signed body, as the change feed's answer does in revision. The adapter refuses an answer that contains another revision than the one it implements and sent, and advances no cursor from it. An answer's signature covers its body and is bound to the request's signature, so the revision that the answer was built for is signed. Each member and each entry kind belongs to the revision of the feed that defines it. An adapter ignores a member of the answer or of an entry that its revision does not define. The must_understand of an entry overrides that for the members it lists, as changes.schema.json describes. An adapter skips and acknowledges a change entry whose kind its revision does not define. It does the same for an entry whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define. It reads the kind and must_understand alone, applies nothing else in the entry, and moves its cursor past it. The exception is a change_request entry, which the adapter reports failed with reason refused (changes-failed.schema.json). The control plane reads the bodies of adapter.schema.json, changes-submitted.schema.json and changes-failed.schema.json by the same rule. It ignores an undefined member of the body, unless the must_understand of the body lists it. It refuses a body whose must_understand lists a pointer that it does not define. An adapter sends only the members of the revision that the control plane implements. The description, the run documents and the documents of the provisioner and machines contracts follow the same rule of must_understand. A writer sends them to a reader that may define fewer members. Each schema describes the rule for its document. The Forager contract makes additions safe in the same way, with lenient answers whose unknown members are ignored. The control plane refuses a time or a timestamp more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, and a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401. That 401 is one uniform answer for everything about who is asking, whose causes refusal.schema.json lists, and nothing in it shows which cause applied. An X-Qory-Access-Key-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519 or X-Qory-Timestamp sent twice, or an X-Qory-Instance-Id that is absent or outside its pattern, is refused 400 bad_request, and only those are. It decodes the signature strictly, as 64 bytes of strict base64url, and verifies it as accesskey's PublicKey.VerifyRequest does, refusing an S at or above the group order. It keys its replay check on the 64 decoded bytes, and keeps each accepted signature until the request's time or X-Qory-Timestamp is more than 300 seconds behind its clock. A retry is a new request: the adapter builds it again, a POST with a time and a GET with an X-Qory-Timestamp later than those of the request it retries, and signs it again. Each GET an instance sends has an X-Qory-Timestamp later than that of the previous GET it sent, so no two GETs of one instance have the same signature, and an answer bound to one GET verifies for no other. A request sent again unchanged has a signature the control plane has seen, and is refused, 401; an adapter never takes that 401 as its access key being revoked. Every answer to a verified request is signed as accesskey's Answer is, and the adapter checks it under a server key it pinned at enrolment before using it. A 401 is always unsigned. A 413, 415 or 400 bad_request may be unsigned, because the control plane may decide them before it verifies the request's signature. Every other answer is signed, and an adapter acts on no other unsigned answer. On an unsigned 401, 413, 415 or 400 bad_request, the adapter changes no state: no cursor, no run, no key. It treats the request as failed and sends it again, built anew as a retry is above, with backoff. It never takes a 401 as revocation, and never splits or drops items because of an unsigned 413. An unsigned 429 is not a 429: the adapter ignores its Retry-After and backs off as it does for any failed request. A POST whose schema defines no answer body is answered, on success, with a signed 204 and no body. A POST whose Content-Type is not application/json is refused 415 unsupported_media_type; a GET has no body and no Content-Type, and is never refused 415. The control plane also calls the adapter, at the call_url the adapter declares in its start-up body (adapter.schema.json), and makes no call to an adapter that declares none. A call is a POST of application/json to call_url followed by the call's path, as given in the call's schema, and its body has a time, as a request's body does. The control plane signs each call with its server key: the headers X-Qory-Adapter-Id, X-Qory-Instance-Id, X-Qory-Contract-Version and X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519, the signature 64 bytes of Ed25519 in base64url without padding, over qory-call-ed25519-v1, the adapter id, the instance id, the method, the call's path as given in its schema, and the raw body, joined by line feeds with none after the last; the body's time is checked for freshness. The signed path is the call's path alone, not the address the call is sent to, so a proxy in front of the adapter may change that address. The adapter id is the id the control plane enrolled the adapter as, the adapter_id of a connect pass, and the instance id is the X-Qory-Instance-Id of the adapter's requests, so a call signed for one adapter, or for one instance of it, verifies at no other. X-Qory-Contract-Version is the revision the control plane built the call for; the adapter refuses one that is missing, sent twice, not a decimal integer, or a revision it does not implement, 400 unsupported_contract_version. The adapter decodes the signature strictly, as 64 bytes of strict base64url, and verifies it under a server key it pinned at enrolment, as accesskey's Pin.Verify does, refusing an S at or above the group order; after a server key rotation it tries each pinned key, and any one that verifies passes. It checks that the adapter id is the id it is enrolled as and that the instance id is the one it sends in its requests. It refuses a call whose time is more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, and a call whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401: one uniform answer for every cause, and nothing in it shows which cause applied. It keys its replay check on the 64 decoded bytes, and keeps each accepted signature until the call's time is more than 300 seconds behind its clock. A retry of a call is a new call: the control plane builds it again, with a later time, and signs it again. The adapter signs its answer to a verified call with its access key: the header X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519, the signature over qory-call-answer-ed25519-v1, the status as three decimal digits, the call's X-Qory-Signature-Ed25519 exactly as sent, and the lower-case hex SHA-256 of the body, joined by line feeds with none after the last, so the answer is bound to the call it answers. The control plane checks the answer under the adapter's live access key before using it. An answer to a call whose content the revision bounds contains that revision in revision, inside its signed body, and the control plane refuses one that contains another revision than the call's X-Qory-Contract-Version. A 401 to a call is always unsigned. The control plane acts on no unsigned answer to a call, and treats it as a failed call. The body of a call and the body of its answer follow the JSON rules of a request's body: an integer has no fraction and no exponent, and no object repeats a member. The adapter refuses a call whose body breaks those rules or its schema, 400 invalid_request, and the control plane refuses an answer that breaks them or its schema. The adapter refuses a call with the body of refusal.schema.json. The domain lines of a call and of its answer are not those of a request, an answer, a pass or a connect return, so no signature of one kind verifies as a signature of another kind. The adapter's access key is the integration's, enrolled once for the instance. An organisation reaches the adapter only through a connection, and no request refers to an organisation or a workspace. The adapter links the access the source grants to a connection only as described in connect-pass.schema.json: the source confirms the grant for the flow that carried the pass, and a grant is linked to at most one live connection. See connection_id under $defs for when a connection is made. A request for a connection that ended, or for a collection that ended with one, is refused, 409 connection_ended, except a sources/disconnect, which is answered with the signed 204 (sources-disconnect.schema.json); the refusal is final for that connection: this is how an end on the control plane's side reaches the adapter. After a connections/disconnect (connections-disconnect.schema.json), or a 409 connection_ended, the adapter drops that connection's collections from its state. A collection_ref resolves to the live collection with that ref; on a sources/disconnect, only to one live under the connection_id in the request (sources-disconnect.schema.json). When none is live, items and comments are answered by the collection with that ref that ended last: 409 connection_ended if it ended with its connection; otherwise, and for a ref the control plane holds no collection for, collection_not_linked. Comments refer to an item by item_ref, not a collection, so for comments the collection that answers is the collection of the item with that item_ref: the live one, or, when none is live, the one that ended last; and for an item_ref the control plane holds no item for, collection_not_linked. When the control plane no longer holds a connection, as after its organisation is removed, a request that contains its connection_id is answered 403 connection_unknown, not connection_ended, except a sources/disconnect, which is answered with the signed 204 (sources-disconnect.schema.json). A connection's collections end when it ends, and a connection the control plane no longer holds has no collections, so none of its refs resolves to a live collection. So an adapter treats a 403 connection_unknown that lasts after its retries as the connection ended, for a live connection (connection_id under $defs), on any request for it, a listing or a connections/disconnect: it drops that connection's collections from its state, as on 409 connection_ended. A 403 forbidden, a request the access key may not make, whatever the connection, never ends a connection. The adapter chooses how many retries, and over what time. A pending link, one with no listing ever accepted, is never dropped by counting 403s: its listing is refused 403 connection_unknown by design until the person's browser delivers the connect return. After it mints a linked connect return, the adapter sends that connection's listing of collections at once, its first listing, and sends it again with backoff while the answer is 403 connection_unknown, until a 204 makes the connection live or the final listing below ends the link; a signed 409 connection_ended to any of those listings drops the link at once. That 403 is expected until the browser delivers the return, and it is not a lasting 403: the adapter keeps sending the listing, with backoff, until the final listing. On a transient failure or an unsigned answer, the adapter sends the listing again, built anew, with backoff. So the adapter learns that a connection is made without waiting for the final listing. Once the connect return it minted for a pending link has expired and 300 seconds more have passed on its clock, the adapter lists that connection once more, its final listing, which for a replaced link is the last of the empty listings described below: a 204 means the connection is made; a 403 connection_unknown or a signed 409 connection_ended drops the link; a signed 409 connection_suspended means the connection is made, since a pending connection is answered 403 connection_unknown before any suspension is decided, so the adapter keeps the link as for a made connection and sends its requests again on its periodic check, as for any suspended connection, or, for a replaced link, ends that connection as described below; a signed 403 forbidden, a request the access key may not make, never ends a connection or drops a link, so the adapter keeps the link and sends the listing again with backoff, as for a transient failure; and a transient failure, no answer, a 429 or a 5xx, or an unsigned answer keeps the link, and the adapter sends the listing again, built anew, with backoff. The 300 seconds cover the clock difference the freshness check allows. A connection has a list of grants, one per external account at the source, and the adapter reports each grant with POST /v1/grants (grant.schema.json), and the end of one grant, when the source no longer covers it, with POST /v1/grants/end (grant-end.schema.json), which ends that grant and its collections and leaves the connection. A newer pass for the same external account (connect-pass.schema.json) replaces that account's grant at once. The control plane accepts a return only for the nonce of the connection's latest pass. Before a flow on another connection replaces a pending link of the same grant, the adapter lists the pending link's connection: a 204 means that connection is made and now live, and the later flow is refused grant_taken; a 403 connection_unknown means it is still pending, and the replacement goes ahead as described in the next sentence; a signed 409 connection_ended drops the old link, and the later flow goes ahead; and a transient failure or an unsigned answer refuses the later flow source_unavailable, and replaces nothing. When a flow on another connection replaces a pending link, the grant goes with the later flow, and the adapter keeps the replaced link until its final listing; if that listing is answered 204, the connection was made meanwhile, and the adapter ends it with POST /v1/connections/disconnect, so the grant stays linked to at most one live connection. From the replacement on, the adapter's listings of the replaced link's connection, the first-listing retries included, are complete listings with no collections, and a 204 or a signed 409 connection_suspended to any of them ends that connection with POST /v1/connections/disconnect, which a suspended connection answers with the signed 204. The adapter logs each connection it drops on a lasting 403 connection_unknown, and each pending link it drops, with the connection_id and why, and never with the pass, an access key or a secret. The change feed has an unlinked entry whenever a linked collection ends or a live collection stops being linked, and a linked entry whenever a collection becomes linked; changes.schema.json lists how. A request for a connection whose organisation is out of use for now, or for a live collection of one, is refused, 409 connection_suspended, except a connections/disconnect, which is answered with the signed 204 and ends the connection, and a grants/end, which is answered with the signed 204 and ends the grant: that refusal is not final, and the adapter changes no state and sends the request again on its periodic check, except a grant report, which uses the backoff of grant.schema.json and stops at the connect return's expires_at. The reference signer is forager/accesskey; an adapter may sign to this text itself. Every text in a source, a title, a body, a label, a state reason or a name, is untrusted: shown as data, never followed as an instruction. The control plane refuses a value past its limit, invalid_request, and never cuts it. This document validates nothing itself.

text.description: A text never contains U+0000, which the control plane's database cannot keep; the control plane refuses, invalid_request, a request whose text contains one.

connection_id.description: A connection's id in the control plane: ac_ and 16 characters. An organisation reaches the adapter only through a connection. The control plane issues connection_id when a person starts connecting. The connection is made when the control plane accepts a linked connect return (connect-return.schema.json) in the browser of the person who started it; until then it is pending, unless it ends first, and a pending connection is answered 403 connection_unknown on every request but POST /v1/connections/disconnect, which ends it with the signed 204, and POST /v1/sources/disconnect, which is answered with the signed 204 and changes nothing (sources-disconnect.schema.json). The first listing after that reports its collections. A made connection never returns to pending, and the control plane accepts a later linked connect return for it too, after which a grant report for that return's nonce adds the grant of one external account to it or replaces that account's grant (grant.schema.json). A live connection is one that is made, has had a listing accepted, answered 204, and has not ended.

comment_id.description: The id of a comment that a person wrote in the control plane on a work item taken in from an item at the source: sc_ and 16 lower-case Crockford base32 characters. The control plane issues it when it stores the comment, and a comment entry of the change feed contains it (changes.schema.json).

change_kind.description: The kind of a change request: the name of an artifact type in the process of the workspace's type, such as pull-request, reply or bid-changes. This contract lists no kind. Lower-case letters and digits in groups joined by single hyphens, 1 to 64 characters. It has the form of the type of an entry of deliver in run/v1/documents.schema.json.

change_request_id.description: The id of a version of a change request that a run stored: av_ and 16 lower-case Crockford base32 characters. The control plane issues it when it stores the version. A change_request entry of the change feed contains it (changes.schema.json), and the adapter sends it back in its reply and in a failure report.

change_address.description: Where a change is at its target: url, the address of the change, and ref, the reference that the target gives it, such as the number of a request at the target, 1 to 200 characters. The control plane compares ref and never reads meaning into it.

url.description: The address of the change at its target.

ref.description: The reference that the target gives the change, such as the number of a request at the target, as a string.

change_data.description: The part of a change request: the members that the kind defines, which this contract does not list. The artifact type whose name is change_kind, in the process of the workspace's type, defines the part of an entry, and the control plane validates the part of an entry against it. This contract states nothing about the part of a reply beyond the limits here. A part has at most 786432 bytes (768 KiB) serialized, which no schema can count: the control plane writes no larger part in an entry and refuses a larger one in a reply, 400 invalid_request. The numbers inside a part follow the schema of the kind, so they may have a fraction or an exponent; no object inside a part repeats a member, at any depth. A schema can express the limits of $defs.change_value, which apply to each value inside a part.

change_value.description: A value inside a part: at most 1024 items in an array, 256 members in an object, 20000 characters in a string, a member name of 1 to 128 characters, and no U+0000 in a string or a name.

change_title.description: The title of a change request of any kind is 1 to 256 characters on one line. It has the character rule of a prose line (description.schema.json, $defs.line): no control character (category Cc: U+0000 to U+001F and U+007F to U+009F), no U+2028 or U+2029, and no format character (category Cf) other than U+200C and U+200D. It has at least one character that is not a space, U+200C or U+200D. A space is U+0020, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+202F, U+205F or U+3000.

time.description: RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds: hours 00 to 23, minutes and seconds 00 to 59, so never a leap second.

ref.description: The adapter's reference to a thing at the source, 1 to 200 characters, stable for that thing. The control plane compares it and stores it, and never reads meaning into it.

environment_ref.description: An id of a collection's environment definition, as the adapter reads it: it changes whenever that definition changes, and is absent when the collection has none. 1 to 200 characters, like a ref; the control plane compares it and stores it, and never reads meaning into it.

url.description: An https URL, at most 2048 characters, as RFC 3986 writes a URI: https://, a host, a port when one is written, then a path, a query and a fragment, each optional. The host is a name of letters, digits, the characters -._~!$&'()*+,;=, the percent-encodings %80 to %FF in either case, and %25, or an IPv6 address in brackets as RFC 3986 writes one, and only a port, a path, a query or a fragment follows the closing bracket; no user information comes before the host. A colon after the host may stand alone, or be followed by a port of at most 5 digits whose value is from 1 to 65535, leading zeros allowed. Every % starts a percent-encoding, % and two hexadecimal digits, and the URL contains no character outside RFC 3986's.

endpoint_url.description: Where an API is: an https URL, at most 2048 characters, of https://, a host, a port when one is written, and a path when one is written, with no user information, no query and no fragment. The host is lower-case labels joined by dots, each label 1 to 63 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens that starts and ends with a letter or a digit. A port is a colon and a decimal number from 1 to 65535, with no leading zero. A path is a / followed by letters, digits, the characters -._~!$&'()*+,;=:@/ and percent-encodings, each % and two hexadecimal digits.

model_id.description: A model's id, exactly as a provider's API takes it: 1 to 200 printable ASCII characters, no space, starting with a letter or a digit.

effort_value.description: An effort value a model accepts, exactly as the provider's API takes it: 1 to 32 characters of lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.

title.description: A title, as it is in the source, 1 to 1024 characters.

body.description: A body text, as it is in the source, at most 65536 characters, possibly empty.

body_format.description: How the body is written: markdown or text, the values a reader knows. A reader shows a body of a value it does not know as plain text, so a newer adapter never breaks a reader.

person.description: Who wrote something at the source: their display name, and whether a person or an automation acts under it.

name.description: The display name the source shows, 1 to 100 characters.

kind.description: person, or automation for an account a program acts under.

labels.description: The source's labels on the thing, as text: at most 100, each 1 to 100 characters, none twice. A reader shows them and acts on none.

state_reason.description: Why the item is in its state, display text the adapter words, at most 64 characters, never a raw value from the source; null when the adapter gives none.

type.description: The adapter's word for what an item is, such as task or bug, stored as data: lower-case letters and spaces, at most 40 characters.

address_path.description: The path of a place in the address of a target: 1 to 200 characters, none of them a control character, U+0000 to U+001F or U+007F.

target.description: Where a change would go: one of the adapter's collections, and, when the place has one, its address on a system.

collection.description: The collection's ref, as the adapter's source-collections.schema.json listed it.

address.description: The address of the place on a system: the host name and the path. Absent when the place has no address, such as a place that is not on a host.

system.description: The host name of the system.

secret_name.description: The name of a secret the adapter stores in the control plane (adapter-secrets.schema.json): 1 to 64 characters of lower-case letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter or a digit. A name is never a value: the adapter names a secret, such as signing-key, and never writes its value into the name.

suite.description: The suite of a sealed value: RFC 9180 base mode with DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) 0x0020, HKDF-SHA256 0x0001 and AES-256-GCM 0x0002, the suite of the Forager contract's secrets answer.

public_key.description: An Ed25519 public key, 32 bytes in base64url without padding, every bit after the last full byte zero.

access_key_id.description: An access key's id: ak_ and 16 lower-case Crockford base32 characters.

enc.description: The encapsulated key of a sealed value: the sender's fresh ephemeral X25519 public key, 32 bytes in base64url without padding, every bit after the last full byte zero.

ct.description: The ciphertext of a sealed value followed by the 16-byte tag, in base64url without padding, every bit after the last full byte zero.

nonce.description: A pass's nonce: 128 random bits in base64url without padding, 22 characters.

domain.description: A kind of work that a workspace is set up for, such as software.

listing.description: One part of a listing: a read of the source, from its start to its end, sent in parts. A listing is complete when every part from 1 to n has arrived and part n has complete: true. An adapter sends complete: true only for a listing whose paging cannot skip an item.

id.description: The listing's id, 1 to 200 characters, the same on each of its parts and new for each listing.

part.description: The part's number, from 1 to 10000, so n, the last part's number, is at most 10000 too.

started_at.description: When the adapter began reading the source for this listing, the same on each of its parts. For a listing of collections, the control plane compares started_at, never the time a part arrives: a collection keeps the started_at of the latest listing of its connection that contained it, a listing that began earlier changes nothing of that collection, and a listing of another connection that began earlier leaves the ref with that collection (source-collections.schema.json).

complete.description: true on the last part alone: parts 1 to this one contain the whole listing. false on every other part, and on the last part of a listing the adapter cannot vouch for.
